slot.brief: Source moving towards and then away from a stationary observer at the same speed; find the ratio of the two observed frequencies or compare with the source frequency.

stem: A source emitting a tone of frequency $500\ \text{Hz}$ moves towards and, after passing, away from a stationary observer at the same speed, $30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. If the speed of sound is $330\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, find the ratio of the observed frequencies before and after passing.

verdicts.working: Before passing: f₁ = 500·330/(330−30) = 550 Hz. After passing: f₂ = 500·330/(330+30) ≈ 458.3 Hz. Thus f₁/f₂ = 6/5.

working:
$\dfrac{f_{\text{toward}}}{f_{\text{away}}}=\dfrac{v/(v-u)}{v/(v+u)}=\dfrac{v+u}{v-u}=\dfrac{330+30}{330-30}=\dfrac{6}{5}$

Independent check: Before passing: f₁ = 500·330/(330−30) = 550 Hz. After passing: f₂ = 500·330/(330+30) ≈ 458.3 Hz. Thus f₁/f₂ = 6/5.
solution:
For a moving source, $f_{\text{toward}}=f\dfrac{v}{v-u}$ and $f_{\text{away}}=f\dfrac{v}{v+u}$. Hence,
$$\dfrac{f_{\text{toward}}}{f_{\text{away}}}=\dfrac{v+u}{v-u}=\dfrac{330+30}{330-30}=\dfrac{6}{5}$$
